gates.claim: the old side condition Re(1-yz)>0 on [0,1] is EXACTLY Re y < 1, so the region it excluded is the whole half-plane Re y >= 1 (minus the cut). On points there -- including both examples qou-clx8 names -- cLiTwoExt still equals Li2, so the old hypothesis was excluding a region where the identity holds, exactly as that bean says
the Lean hypothesis `y.im != 0 or y.re < 1` is exactly C minus [1,inf): it rejects every point of the cut and accepts every point off it

the cut is [1,inf) and not |y|>=1 because for real y>1 the integrand is singular INSIDE the interval, at z = 1/y in (0,1) -- that is the actual obstruction, and it is what makes the geometric hypothesis the right one

cLiTwoExt(t*y) = -int_0^t log(1-y u)/u du -- the substitution u = t*z, which moves the parameter OUT of the integrand and INTO the limit of integration. This is what lets FTC reach it instead of differentiation under the integral
d/dt cLiTwoExt(t*y) = -log(1 - y*t)/t -- the radial derivative the Lean file proves by the fundamental theorem of calculus. Finite-difference check at step 1e-12 (central, so error ~ h^2 * f''')

the radial statement is the chain-rule reading of d/dw Li2(w) = -log(1-w)/w: cLiTwoExt'(t y)*y = -log(1-y t)/t identically. So G5 is that derivative restricted to rays, not a weaker statement about a different function

the quadrature trap qou-clx8 records is REAL and is mitigated here: at y = 3 + 0.001i plain quad([0,1]) is silently wrong, while splitting at Re(1/y) is exact. Demonstrated rather than asserted, so every other gate's method is visible

verdict.outcome: cLiTwoExt's integral converges on ALL of C minus [1,inf) -- the geometric hypothesis qou-clx8 asked for, now Lean-proved -- and its derivative ALONG RAYS is proved by FTC rather than by differentiating under the integral sign.
verdict.what_widened: the old side condition Re(1-y)>0 rejects every point in G1, including both examples the bean names, while the identity holds at all of them. ComplexDilogarithm.intervalIntegrable_log_one_sub_div is now stated on slitPlane membership, with the old form kept as a corollary.
verdict.still_open: full analyticity on C minus [1,inf) needs the derivative in EVERY direction, not just radially. The natural next route is a primitive-of-a-holomorphic-function argument on the simply connected slit plane (Mathlib has Analysis/Complex/HasPrimitives.lean); it is NOT written. So 'the analytic continuation' is still a name plus agreement-on-the-disc plus this radial derivative.
verdict.does_not_move_the_sum_rule: qou-clx8 is explicit that Route 5 is a restatement; even the whole chain leaves an unevaluated real integral. Taken for the Mathlib gap, as instructed.
